मनुष्यजन्ममें सत्संग मिल जाय, गीता - जैसे ग्रन्थसे
परिचय हो जाय, भगवन्नामसे परिचय हो जाय तो
साधकको यह समझना चाहिये कि भगवान्ने बहुत
विशेषतासे कृपा कर दी है; अतः अब तो हमारा उद्धार
होगा ही, अब आगे हमारा जन्म-मरण नहीं होगा । कारण
कि अगर हमारा उद्धार नहीं होना होता, तो ऐसा मौका
नहीं मिलता। परन्तु ‘भगवान्‌की कृपासे उद्धार होगा ही

और उत्साहपूर्वक साधनमें लगे रहना चाहिये । समय
सार्थक बने, कोई समय खाली न जाय - ऐसी सावधानी
हरदम रखनी चाहिये। परन्तु अपने कल्याणकी चिन्ता नहीं
करनी चाहिये; क्योंकि अबतक जिसने इतना प्रबन्ध किया

वाले प्राणी भोगते ही हैं, फिर मनुष्यमें और उन प्राणियों में
क्या फरक रहेगा ? भगवान्‌का कृपा करके मनुष्यशरीर

‘वासुदेवः सर्वम्’२ – महासर्गके आदिमें एक भगवान्
अनेक रूपोंमें हो जाते हैं – 'सदैक्षत बहु स्यां
प्रजायेयेति' (छान्दोग्य० ६ । २ । ३) और अन्तमें अर्थात्
महाप्रलयमें एक भगवान् ही शेष रह जाते हैं - 'शिष्यते
शेषसंज्ञः ' ( श्रीमद्भा० १० । ३ । २५) । इस प्रकार जब आदि
और अन्तमें एक भगवान् ही रहते हैं, तब बीचमें दूसरा
कहाँसे आया ? क्योंकि संसारकी रचना करनेमें भगवान्के
पास अपने सिवाय कोई सामग्री नहीं थी, वे तो स्वयं संसारके
रूपसे प्रकट हुए हैं । इसलिये यह सब वासुदेव ही है। ।
जो चीज आदि और अन्तमें होती है, वही चीज मध्यमें
१- ( १ ) लब्ध्वा सुदुर्लभमिदं बहुसम्भवान्ते मानुष्यमर्थदमनित्यमपीह धीरः ।
तूर्णं यतेत न पतेदनुमृत्युयावन्निःश्रेयसाय विषयः खलु सर्वतः स्यात् ॥ ( श्रीमद्भा० ११ । ९ । २९ )
'अनेक जन्मोंके बाद इस परमपुरुषार्थके साधनरूप मनुष्यशरीरको, जो अनित्य होनेपर भी अत्यन्त दुर्लभ है, पाकर
बुद्धिमान् पुरुषको चाहिये कि वह शीघ्र - से- शीघ्र, मृत्यु आनेसे पहले ही अपने कल्याणके लिये प्रयत्न कर ले । विषयभोग
तो सभी योनियोंमें प्राप्त हो सकते हैं, इसलिये उनके संग्रहमें इस अमूल्य जीवनको नहीं खोना चाहिये । '
(२) नृदेहमाद्यं सुलभं सुदुर्लभं प्लवं सुकल्पं गुरुकर्णधारम् ।
मयानुकूलेन नभस्वतेरितं पुमान् भवाब्धिं न तरेत् स आत्महा ॥ ( श्रीमद्भा० ११ । २० । १७ )
'यह मनुष्यशरीर समस्त शुभ फलोंकी प्राप्तिका मूल है और अत्यन्त दुर्लभ होनेपर भी अनायास सुलभ हो गया है।
इस संसारसागरसे पार होनेके लिये यह एक सुदृढ़ नौका है, जिसे गुरुरूप नाविक चलाता है और मैं (भगवान्) वायुरूप
होकर इसे लक्ष्यकी ओर बढ़ाने में सहायता देता हूँ । इतनी सुविधा होनेपर भी जो मनुष्य इस संसारसागरसे पार नहीं होता, वह
अपनी आत्माका हनन करनेवाला अर्थात् पतन करनेवाला है । '
२- यहाँ 'वासुदेवः' शब्द पुंल्लिंगमें और 'सर्वम्' शब्द नपुंसकलिंगमें आया है । यहाँ 'वासुदेवः सर्वः ' भी कह सकते थे;
परन्तु ऐसा न कहकर 'वासुदेवः सर्वम्' कहा है। इसका तात्पर्य यह है कि 'सर्वम्' शब्दमें स्त्री, पुरुष, नपुंसक, स्थावर-जंगम
आदि सबका समाहार हो जाता है ।

The Bhagavad Gita:

[Chapter 7, Third Shloka]. In this way, the practice of Karma Yoga, Jnana Yoga, and Bhakti Yoga - as long as the means of sustenance come, so long we attain them. The implication is that the ultimate human birth has been obtained only for the sake of one's own well-being.

If one gets the association of the righteous (Sat Sang), gets familiar with scriptures like the Gita, and gets familiar with the name of God, then the seeker should understand that God has bestowed His special mercy upon him. Therefore, now our salvation is certain, and there will be no more birth and death. Because if our salvation was not going to happen, then such an opportunity would not have arisen. However, one should not rely solely on the mercy of God, but rather remain vigilant and enthusiastic in one's practice. One should always be mindful of not wasting time and should not be idle at any time. But one should not worry about one's own well-being; because whatever has been arranged so far will continue to be arranged in the future. Just as someone who has invited you to eat, has laid out the seat, has seated you, has placed the plate, and has kept the water in a cup nearby, you should not worry about whether that person will give you food or not. Because if they were not going to give you food, then why would they have invited you, prepared the food, and seated you? But since they have done all this, they will have to give you food. Similarly, God has given us the human body and has arranged all the means for our salvation, so our salvation is certain, and now we have reached the shore of the ocean of the world - one should have this firm faith and engage in practice with a sense of detachment.

If one believes that only those who have good karma in their past lives can approach God, then it would mean that those who have good or bad karma in their past lives are born in animal, bird, insect, or worm forms and suffer the consequences of their karma. Then what difference would there be between humans and other living beings? And what would be the significance of God bestowing the human form upon us? The uniqueness and greatness of the human form lie in the fact that humans can take refuge in God and follow the path of their own well-being.

'Vasudeva is all' - In the beginning of the creation, God manifests Himself in many forms - 'Sadaikshat bahusyam prajayeyeti' (Chandogya Upanishad 6.2.3), and at the end of the creation, only one God remains - 'Shishyate sheshasamjnah' (Shrimad Bhagavatam 10.3.25). Since God remains as the beginning and the end, then where did the middle one come from? Because God did not have any other material to create the universe, He Himself manifested as the universe. Therefore, everything is Vasudeva.

Whatever exists at the beginning and the end, that same thing exists in the middle - 

(1) 'Having obtained this human body, which is extremely difficult to obtain, even though it is impermanent, a wise person should strive to attain his goal before death, because death is inevitable and worldly pleasures are available in all forms of life.' (Shrimad Bhagavatam 11.9.29)

(2) 'This human body is the first and easiest to obtain, but it is extremely difficult to obtain, and it is a suitable and precious gift. A person who is guided by a guru and is carried by the wind (i.e., God) should not drown in the ocean of the world, but rather cross it. If he fails to do so, he will be his own destroyer.' (Shrimad Bhagavatam 11.20.17)

Here, the word 'Vasudeva' is in the masculine form, and the word 'sarvam' is in the neuter form. The phrase 'Vasudeva sarvam' could also be written as 'Vasudeva sarva', but it has been written as 'Vasudeva sarvam'. The implication is that the word 'sarvam' encompasses all living beings, including men, women, and animals.
